description: EngIntel's own package architecture (dogfood, research doc 03). Draft: not enforced until reviewed by the architecture owners and set to active.

layers.description: Shared types, schemas, loaders, and path rules. Depends on no other EngIntel package.
Repository readers: the scanner and the TypeScript parse and symbol passes.
The dependency-cruiser adapter, module graph, and cycle detection.
Pure rule evaluation, diagnostics, and violation identity. No I/O.
The analysis pipeline shared by every surface.
Entry points: the CLI, the GitHub Action, and the MCP server.
Golden fixture loading and test helpers. Never shipped.
Package tests, workspace scripts, and root tool configuration.

rules.comment: Everything depends on the foundation, so it depends on nothing else in EngIntel.
Analysis produces facts; it never judges them or knows who called it.
Rule evaluation is a pure function of the graph, the contract, and an injected clock. Reading files belongs to the readers, wiring to the orchestrator.
One pipeline serves the CLI, the Action, and MCP alike; it must not know which one is calling.
The merge authority (the Action's required check) and the agent-facing MCP server share only the orchestrator (research doc 03, section 8).
Test helpers and fixtures never ship.
dependency-cruiser's JSON never leaves the graph adapter, so the extractor can be replaced without touching the validator (D-001).
Argument parsing belongs to entry points.
The agent is never the authority: no model calls anywhere in EngIntel, including tests and CI.
Module cycles hide ownership and make the pipeline order ambiguous.
Every import must resolve to a file or an installed package.

unlayered.comment: New top-level code should join a layer, or the contract should say why it does not.
